claims.text: Anago rice and oyster set meals are seasoned in the regional style, which relies on wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
The kitchen centers on conger eel, oysters and other seafood, so vegan diners should not assume any shared equipment or stock is free of animal products.

name: 出汁とおでん わいく (Dashi to Oden Waiku)

claims.text: Oden is simmered in a single shared dashi pot seasoned with soy-sauce-based broth, so items share the same wheat-containing liquid.
The cuisine relies on dashi and soy-sauce seasoning typical of Japanese oden and sashimi; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. No wheat-free soy sauce is documented.
The house dashi is made with bonito (fish) and chicken bone in addition to kelp and shiitake, so even vegetable oden items are cooked in an animal-based stock.
Core dish is wheat noodles seasoned with a miso and soy-sauce base, so gluten is integral and there is no documented gluten-free handling.
The broth/seasoning is built on soy sauce (typically wheat-containing) layered with miso.
Signature noodles are topped with miso-seasoned minced meat; no vegan preparation is documented.

name: 電光石火 駅前ひろば店 (Denko-Sekka Ekimae Hiroba)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is made from a wheat-flour batter and topped with wheat noodles, all cooked on a single shared teppan griddle alongside every other order, so cross-contact with wheat is unavoidable.
Dishes are finished with okonomiyaki sauce, a wheat-based Worcester-style sauce; no wheat-free or gluten-free sauce is documented.
The shared griddle is used continuously for pork, egg, squid, oysters, and other animal ingredients, so any item would have animal-product cross-contact.
As a Japanese shellfish izakaya, dishes are expected to use wheat-based Japanese soy sauce and standard seasonings; no gluten-free soy sauce is mentioned.
The menu is built entirely around shellfish and seafood; the house states that those who dislike shellfish will find nothing to eat, so no plant-only meal is offered.
The owner's site asks guests to review allergy and disliked-ingredient information before booking, indicating allergies can be discussed at reservation by phone or LINE.
Cooking fats are limited to extra-virgin olive oil and plant-based safflower oil with low trans-fat content, and the kitchen avoids chemical seasonings and preservatives.

name: ふじの茶屋 里の店 (Fuji no Chaya Sato no Mise)

claims.text: The anago bowl is served with a sweet soy-based tare, which in this style of dish is wheat-containing soy sauce; no allergen information is published.

name: 藤い屋 宮島本店 (Fujiiya Miyajima Honten)

claims.text: The entire product line is wheat-flour-based (castella-batter momiji manju and a wheat/rice/mochi 'momiji mochi'), so the shop is not a gluten-free environment and no allergen-segregated preparation is documented.
Momiji manju batter is a wheat-and-egg castella; custard cream and chocolate fillings are also not plant-based, and no vegan version is documented.
Momiji manju are made fresh on-site and the shop emphasizes no preservatives and carefully selected ingredients.

name: 袋町ワイン食堂 LE JYAN JYAN (Fukuromachi Wine Shokudo LE JYAN JYAN (Le Jy)

claims.text: Kitchen makes a point of using fresh vegetables from contract and own farms, so plant-based plates are part of the everyday menu.
